artifacts.summary: Confirms both defects (unnormalized class grouping; silent last-wins repeated --tasks flag) against the live script, grounds the canonical 'scope excursion' spelling in two already-hardcoded call sites, surveys 859 distinct raw class strings across the full issues.jsonl corpus, enumerates the 8 files a seed-enum promotion must touch, and recommends a mechanical-fold-now / alias-table-mechanism-but-empty / length-based-1d-warning design with rejected alternatives recorded.

memory_candidates.content: orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh's issue-log class vocabulary: 'scope excursion' (lowercase, single space) is already the literal --class string hardcoded at two mechanical call sites (git-commit-phase.sh:741, git-commit-scoped.sh:866), accounting for 443 of ~3800 corpus-wide issues.jsonl lines -- the most frequent class by far. Promoting a seed class touches 8 files total (3 hold the actual list: issue-log.md, issue-record.sh, orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh; 5 more restate the '17-class' count in prose, including the literal text orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh injects into every generated dispatch file).

When designing a near-duplicate-class normalizer: mechanical case+separator folding (ascii_downcase + hyphen/underscore/space fold) is safe to apply unconditionally because it only ever merges strings built from the SAME words; a curated semantic-alias table for different-word near-synonyms (e.g. 'design-gap' vs 'design-ambiguity') should ship as an empty, documented mechanism rather than pre-populated, since thin evidence (1 corpus occurrence each) and opposite-direction false near-duplicates (a 'scope omission' class is the opposite of a 'scope excursion' class despite sharing the word 'scope') make silent semantic merging risky.

A length/verb-keyword heuristic for detecting a free-text 'sentence' masquerading as a short enum value should prefer token-count-after-fold over a verb/keyword blocklist: this repo's own issue-log corpus already uses many short, legitimate, verb-bearing class names ('hypothesis confirmed', 'fix confirmed working', 'mechanism confirmed', 'blocker-cleared', 'tooling worked first try'), so a keyword blocklist on words like 'confirmed'/'found'/'discovered' would false-positive heavily against live, idiomatic usage.
